criteria.criterion: Grep of .github/workflows/ci.yml shows separate jobs for fmt, clippy and a test job with `strategy.matrix` of 6 shards, plus a job with `name: ci` whose `needs` lists fmt, clippy and the test job and which uses `if: always()` and fails when any needed result is not success; every job has `timeout-minutes`.
criteria.evidence: I read the diff. ci.yml has these jobs: `gate`, `fmt`, `clippy`, `test` (`strategy.fail-fast: false`, `matrix.shard: [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5]`, each shard runs `cargo run --locked -p xtask -- test-shard ${{ matrix.shard }} 6`), `pass`, and `ci` (`name: ci`, `needs: [gate, fmt, clippy, test]`, `if: always()`). The `ci` script exits 1 unless the gate succeeded and each check is `success`, or `skipped` when gate.outputs.skip is 'true'. Every job has timeout-minutes, including history, attribution and pr-head, which each got 30. Tests `workflow_jobs_are_separate_sharded_and_gated_by_ci`, `workflow_jobs_reject_a_missing_gate_condition_need_or_timeout` and `workflow_ci_job_is_green_only_when_every_check_succeeded` pass. The last one runs the real ci script under sh for the success, failure, cancelled and skipped combinations.

criteria.criterion: All `uses:` lines in ci.yml remain pinned by 40-hex commit SHA, the three cache layers (toolchain, registry, target) and the D121 fingerprint/ci-pass lookup, gate and mark steps are still present, and the pass marker is saved only after all checks succeeded.
criteria.evidence: Every new `uses:` line in the diff reuses one of the existing SHA pins (checkout 3d3c42e…, cache restore and save 5a3ec84…). `workflow_actions_are_pinned` passes; it finds at least 20 `uses:` lines and requires @[0-9a-f]{40} on each. fmt, clippy and test each restore and save the toolchain (rustup-), registry (registry-) and target (target-fmt-/target-clippy-/target-test-) caches, and the saves stay default-branch-only. `gate` keeps the fingerprint, lookup (ci-pass), decide and report steps. `pass` has `needs: [gate, fmt, clippy, test]` and no `if`, so it runs only when all of them succeeded; it alone runs `ci-cache mark` and saves `ci-pass`. The re-pointed policy tests (12) and `workflow_caches_keep_three_layers_in_each_check_job` pass.

criteria.criterion: An xtask test reads .github/workflows/ci.yml, extracts each shard's test command and the shard count, and fails when the shards do not partition the workspace test targets exactly once; run `cargo test -p xtask` and see it pass, and a negative case inside the test (a mutated shard list with a dropped or duplicated shard) is shown to fail the check.
criteria.evidence: 18 of 18 tests pass. `shards_in_ci_yml_partition_every_workspace_test_target` parses the matrix list and n from the real ci.yml, runs the built `xtask test-shard k n --dry-run` for each k, and compares the result with a cargo-metadata oracle. `oracle_matches_files_on_disk` cross-checks that oracle against the source files. `partition_rejects_a_changed_shard_list` asserts that a dropped shard, a duplicated shard, a shard past n, a changed n, a hard-coded k and a missing list are each rejected. The cover-only negatives (a unit in no shard, a unit in two shards, a unit twice in one shard, an extra oracle unit, a ghost unit) each return Err naming the unit.

criteria.criterion: `cargo run -p xtask -- test-shard <k> <n>` exists; for n=6 and k in 0..5 (or the documented index base) the selected targets are disjoint and their union equals the target set of `cargo test --workspace`; a test in xtask asserts this, and invalid k/n (k>=n, n=0) exits with an error. Run `cargo test -p xtask`.
criteria.evidence: `test-shard 0 1 --dry-run` lists 57 sorted units: every lib, the doctests of each lib, athena-cli's renamed `--bin athena`, xtask's bin, and every integration-test file. `test_shard_6_is_disjoint_and_equals_the_workspace_target_set` and `test_shard_1_equals_the_workspace` pass, and the 6 shard unit tests pass. `test-shard 6 6` exits 1 with 'error: <k> must be below <n>'. `test-shard 0 0` exits 1 with 'error: <n> must be at least 1'. A real (non-dry) run of `test-shard 56 57` ran `cargo test --locked -p xtask --test walltime`, and its 6 tests passed. Shards are numbered from 0, as the docs say. The workspace has no default-members, so `cargo test` equals `cargo test --workspace`.

findings.summary: The landing wait in athena-core still names the old check run `fmt, clippy, tests`, which this change removes.
findings.evidence: `EARLY_RUN_JOB: &str = "fmt, clippy, tests"` sits under a comment that says 'It must match the job name in the CI workflow'. After this change that job name no longer exists, so the wait returns at once with 'no check run', and a landing run can miss the cached D121 pass. Correctness holds (the landing run's own CI decides), so this only weakens a speed optimization. The file is outside the request's Files list, and the producer recorded the effect in CHANGELOG and ci-routing.md §4.4 as a follow-up (name the `pass` job). No test catches the mismatch, so the follow-up should be scheduled.

findings.summary: Three changed files are not on the expected deliverables list.
findings.evidence: The diff stat shows changes to ci_cache.rs (doc comment, and report text 'fmt, clippy, tests:' → 'gate:'), fingerprint.rs (a doc comment) and policy.rs (D121 tests re-pointed from the removed `checks` job to `gate`/`pass`/check jobs). All three were in the planned files and sit under xtask/, which the request's Files allow. The policy.rs change is needed because those tests read the job that was removed. Each is small and directly caused by the job rename.

findings.summary: The partition oracle models cargo's target rules from cargo metadata rather than observing what `cargo test --workspace` actually runs.
findings.evidence: The oracle is written independently of shard.rs and is cross-checked against the source files on disk, but it encodes the same model: a target with `test == true`, lib/bin/test kinds, and one --doc unit per lib with doctests. A rule both copies get wrong (for example targets with required-features, of which this workspace has none, verified by grep) would pass. A stronger later check would compare against `cargo test --workspace -- --list` output. This is acceptable for now; the producer documented why it chose this approach.

findings.summary: Shards 1–5 get only a partial warm target cache, and per-unit cargo invocations can resolve features differently from one --workspace run.
findings.evidence: Only shard 0 saves `target-test-…`, so the other shards restore shard 0's build. Each unit runs as a separate `cargo test -p <pkg> <selector>`. Both are disclosed as known effects for the throughput review. They may reduce the speedup but do not affect correctness.

summary: The change does what the request asks. ci.yml now runs fmt, clippy and a 6-shard test matrix as separate jobs after a `gate` job that keeps the D121 fingerprint, lookup and decision. A `pass` job writes the marker only when all checks succeeded. A final `ci` job with `if: always()` fails unless every check succeeded, or was skipped because the gate reused a pass. Every job has timeout-minutes, and every action stays SHA-pinned. `xtask test-shard <k> <n>` (0-based, with --dry-run) splits the workspace's test targets using cargo metadata. I ran it: it lists 57 units, rejects `6 6` and `0 0` with an error, and a real single-unit run executed and passed its tests. The new ci_shards tests (18/18) read the real ci.yml, check that the shards cover every target exactly once, and reject both mutated shard lists and wrong shard sets. The re-pointed policy tests (12/12) and Athena's recorded fmt, clippy and full test runs (1810 tests) pass. The CHANGELOG and docs say the run time is not measured and leave it to the throughput review. There are four minor findings. The main one: athena-core's `EARLY_RUN_JOB` still names the removed `fmt, clippy, tests` check, so landing runs can miss the cached pass until a follow-up changes that file, which this request did not allow. The producer documented it. The others: three changed xtask files are not on the deliverables list (all in the plan and needed for the rename), the partition oracle is model-based, and the shard cache is only partly warm. None of these blocks the change.
